<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915244_theRebbe_950" batchId="chunked-post-1783581047769-part-005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>When Torah study lacks the awareness that it is God's Torah, it can lead to divisiveness rather than peace, as illustrated by a story of a scholar who complained to the Tzemach Tzedek about being trampled upon.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And from the continuation of the topics in the maamar, it is understood,</t>
    <t s="1">that when the study of Torah is not in this manner,</t>
    <t s="2">then,</t>
    <t s="3">(in addition to the fact that it does not bring peace to the world)</t>
    <t s="4">it is possible that it will bring about division of hearts,</t>
    <t s="5">the opposite of peace.</t>
    <t s="6">For when he lacks the feeling that the Torah is the Torah of Havayah,</t>
    <t s="7">then,</t>
    <t s="8">he takes credit for himself that he studied much Torah43</t>
    <t s="9">and becomes a tangible entity that considers himself a man of virtue and an important person,</t>
    <t s="10">and this causes division of hearts,</t>
    <t s="11">for from the perspective of his selfhood he thinks that everything another says or does is in order to oppose him.</t>
    <t s="12">And as the story</t>
    <t s="13">(cited in the maamar44),</t>
    <t s="14">that someone</t>
    <t s="15">(a great intellectual in scholarship)</t>
    <t s="16">came to the Tzemach Tzedek for a yechidus and complained, "They are stepping on me in the study hall,"</t>
    <t s="17">and the Tzemach Tzedek answered him,</t>
    <t s="18">"You are spreading yourself over the entire study hall,</t>
    <t s="19">so wherever that one steps, it is all on you."</t>
    <t s="20">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="21">that this which the maamar brings, that his claim was that they were trampling on him in the study hall,</t>
    <t s="22">[indicates that] although the study hall is a microcosmic Sanctuary45,</t>
    <t s="23">for the indwelling of the Shechinah in the microcosmic Sanctuary is akin to the indwelling of the Shechinah in the Holy Temple46,</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="25">even there there was the extension of his selfhood.</t>
    <t s="26">And the maamar specifies,</t>
    <t s="27">that this complaint before the Tzemach Tzedek that they were trampling on him was when he was in yechidus,</t>
    <t s="28">for the matter of yechidus is the connection of the Yechidah of the one entering for yechidus with the Yechidah of the Rebbe to whom he entered47,</t>
    <t s="29">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="30">even when he was in yechidus, he had the feeling that they were trampling on him.</t>
    <t s="31">And therefore the maamar brings the above details of the story,</t>
    <t s="32">in order to emphasize that through intellect alone,</t>
    <t s="33">without avodah,</t>
    <t s="34">it is possible for the extension of selfhood to exist even in a microcosmic Sanctuary and even when entering into yechidus,</t>
    <t s="35">from which is understood the necessity of the matter of avodah.</t>
    <t s="36">And afterwards the Tzemach Tzedek told him the explanation of the verse48</t>
    <t s="37">"Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts,"</t>
    <t s="38">"on" (און)</t>
    <t s="39">(with a cholam)</t>
    <t s="40">is strength and power49,</t>
    <t s="41">and the explanation of "man of iniquity" is a man strong in his own opinion.</t>
    <t s="42">And this is "Let the wicked forsake his way and the man of iniquity his thoughts,"</t>
    <t s="43">that just as "let the wicked forsake his way" is something necessary,</t>
    <t s="44">for without teshuvah it is impossible to approach the holy,</t>
    <t s="45">so too it is necessary that the man of iniquity forsake his thoughts</t>
    <t s="46">(the thoughts of selfhood).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The plural "thoughts" indicates that there are many levels of the thought of selfhood, and even the subtlest thought of a Torah scholar can be a barrier, like a speck of dirt on a garment.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that what is written "his thoughts" in the plural,</t>
    <t s="2">it is,</t>
    <t s="3">for in the thought of selfhood there are several levels,</t>
    <t s="4">and therefore it is said "let him forsake... his thoughts" in the plural,</t>
    <t s="5">that he must forsake the subtle thought,</t>
    <t s="6">and even the most subtle of the subtle.</t>
    <t s="7">And to note,</t>
    <t s="8">from the statement of our sages, of blessed memory50,</t>
    <t s="9">regarding the matter of a speck on a garment that interposes regarding immersion,</t>
    <t s="10">that [a speck] of a builder</t>
    <t s="11">[these are Torah scholars who engage in the building of the world]</t>
    <t s="12">[interposes] on one side, and of a boor on two sides.</t>
    <t s="13">For from this it is understood also regarding a spiritual speck,</t>
    <t s="14">that in a Torah scholar even a subtle thought interposes,</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore it is necessary that he forsake "his thoughts" in the plural.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The beginning of avodah is self-nullification, which enables both the upward approach through prayer and the downward approach through Torah study, and the peace of Torah scholars includes the peace of prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is explained in the maamar51,</t>
    <t s="1">that the beginning of avodah is self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="2">For in order to draw near to Elokus,</t>
    <t s="3">both in the aspect of approach from below upward to ascend from level to level in prayer, and in the aspect of approach from above downward in the attainment of Elokus in his soul through Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">it is through humility and lowliness.</t>
    <t s="5">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="6">that this which the maamar specifies the two manners of approach to Elokus,</t>
    <t s="7">although in order to explain the language of the Targum "Alfin b'Oraisa d'Havayah" it seemingly only relates to the approach through Torah,</t>
    <t s="8">it is in order to hint that through the precedence of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="9">the peace of "Your children,"</t>
    <t s="10">Torah scholars who engage in Torah</t>
    <t s="11">(from above downward),</t>
    <t s="12">is in perfection,</t>
    <t s="13">that it also includes the virtue of the peace of prayer</t>
    <t s="14">(from below upward)52.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
